name: City Council Meeting - Aug 20, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  AUGUST 20, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  IN COUNCIL CHAMBER AT 3031 TORRANCE BL.

  CITY COUNCIL MAY TAKE ACTION ON ANY ITEM LISTED ON THE AGENDA

City Council Agenda 08-20-24

OPENING CEREMONIES

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  ROLL CALL
  : Councilmembers Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Sheikh, and Mayor Chen

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  14A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code
  §54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  1. Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees
  2. Certain Part-Time Hourly Employees
  3. Crossing Guards
  4. Elected Officials
  5. Engineers and Torrance Fiscal Employees Association
  6. Executive & Management Employees
  7. Police & Fire Trainees
  8. Safety Management Employees
  9. Torrance City Employees Association
  10. Fire Safety Management
  11. Torrance Fire Fighters Association
  12. Torrance Library Employees Association
  13. Torrance Municipal Employees/AFSCME Local 1117 AFL-CIO
  14. Torrance Police Commanders Association (TPCA)
  15. Torrance Police Officers Association
  16. Torrance Professional Parks & Recreation Employees Organization
  17. Torrance Professional & Supervisory Association
  18. Torrance Recurrent Recreational Employees Organization
  19. City Treasurer
  20. City Attorney
  21. City Manager
  14A - STAFF REPORT

  14B. REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code §54956.8):
  1)  Property: 3511-3525 Pacific Coast Highway, Torrance, CA 90505 Agency Negotiator:
  Aram Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and JAS Madison LLC Under
  Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION

RECONVENED IN PUBLIC SESSION

2.  FLAG SALUTE: Councilmember Lewis NON-SECTARIAN INVOCATION:
  Councilmember Mattucci
 3.  REPORT OF THE CITY CLERK ON THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA The agenda was
  posted on the Public Notice Board at 3031 Torrance Bl. and on the City’s Website on
  Thursday, August 15, 2024 /s/ Rebecca Poirier
  3 - AFFIDAVIT

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES AFTER
NUMBER & TITLE – See Council Rules of Order Section 2.11 (Resolution 2006-65)

4.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS

  6A. RESOLUTION NO. 2024-59 honoring Luz Fierro upon her retirement from the City
  of Torrance after twenty-one years of service. (For Presentation)
  6A - STAFF REPORT
  6A - SUPPLEMENTAL

  6B. PROCLAMATION honoring Torrance Centenarian Joseph H. Gerson.
  6B - STAFF REPORT

7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #1 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comments on items under the Consent Calendar or items that
  are not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on
  items raised during public comment, but may respond briefly to statements made or
  questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals
  are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no
  longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you step up to the microphone. If
  presenting handout material to Council, please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk
  before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you speak.
  PUBLIC COMMENT
  PUBLIC COMMENT RECEIVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 8/19/24 and before 11:04 p.m. on
  8/20/24

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

  8A. Human Resources – Approve Proposed Job Description for Capital Projects
  Construction Superintendent. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Human Resources Director that City Council approve the proposed
  job description for the Capital Projects Construction Superintendent.
  8A - STAFF REPORT

9.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  9A. City Manager and Community Services – Adopt RESOLUTION Approving Deed
  Restriction for City-owned Property Located at 2001 Santa Fe Ave, Commonly
  Known as Torrance Park. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager and Community Services Director that City Council
  adopt a RESOLUTION approving a Deed Restriction to and for the benefit of California
  Natural Resources Agency for a 2018 Parks Bond Act Per Capita Grant Program Award on
  City-owned property located at 2001 Santa Fe Ave, commonly known as Torrance Park
  (APN: 7357-006-900).
  9A - STAFF REPORT

  9B. City Manager – Appoint City Manager, Finance Director, and Deputy Finance
  Director as Authorized Agents of the City of Torrance to Engage in Matters with
  the Federal Emergency Management Agency and California Governor’s Office of
  Emergency Services and Adopt RESOLUTION Appointing the City Manager,
  Finance Director, and Deputy Finance Director as Authorized Agents.
   Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Appoint City Manager, Finance Director, and Deputy Finance Director as authorized
  agents of the City of Torrance to engage in matters with the Federal Emergency
  Management Agency and California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services; and
  2) Adopt RESOLUTION appointing the City Manager, Finance Director, and Deputy
  Finance Director as authorized agents.
  9B - STAFF REPORT
  9B - SUPPLEMENTAL

9C. City Manager and Fire – Accept and File Update Regarding Impacts of COVID-19
  Pandemic on Long-Term Health Care Facilities Located in the City of Torrance.
  Expenditure: None. In response to a follow-up request by Councilmember
  Bridgett Lewis, it is the recommendation of the City Manager and Fire Chief that
  City Council accept and file an update regarding the impacts of the COVID-19
  pandemic on Long-Term Health Care Facilities located in the City of Torrance.
  9C - STAFF REPORT
  9C - STAFF PRESENTATION

9D. City Council Transportation Committee – Accept and File August 6, 2024 Meeting
  Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Council Transportation Committee that City Council accept and
  file August 6, 2024 City Council Transportation Committee Meeting Minutes.
  9D - STAFF REPORT

9E.  Transit – Approve Contract Services Agreement for Rubber Wheel Trolleys as a
  Cooperative Purchase. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed $3,061,083.26. (Non-General
  Fund).
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council approve a contract services
  agreement with Hometown Manufacturing Incorporated of Crandon, WI, as a cooperative
  purchase with the State of Georgia (agreement no. 99999-SPD-SPD0000212-0002) in the
  amount of $3,001,062.02 and authorize a 2% contingency in the amount of $60,021.24, for
  a total not-to-exceed amount of $3,061,083.26, for the purchase and delivery of (10) rubber
  wheel trolley buses for the period beginning August 20, 2024 and ending August 31, 2025.
  9E - STAFF REPORT

9F.  Transit – Authorize Submission of Fiscal Year 2023-24 Federal Transit
  Administration Grant Application and Appropriate Funds. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council:
  1) Authorize the submission and execution of the Transit Department’s Fiscal Year 2023-
  24 Federal Transit Administration, Urbanized Formula (Section 5307) grant application
  in the amount of $4,078,040; and
  2) Appropriate $4,078,040 to a newly established grant project for the purchase of
  replacement buses.
  9F - STAFF REPORT

9G. Transit – Approve Transit Department’s Submittal of Annual Claim for
  Transportation Development Act and State Transit Assistance Funds for Fiscal
  Year 2024-25. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council approve the Transit Department's
  submittal of the annual claim to the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (Metro) for $8,742,281 in Transportation Development Act funds and $1,747,993 in
  State Transit Assistance funds for fiscal year 2024-25.
  9G - STAFF REPORT

9H. Transit – Approve Contract Services Agreements for Compressed Natural Gas
  and Zero Emission Buses as a Cooperative Purchase. Expenditure: Not-to-
  Exceed $23,908,922.75 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council:
  1) Approve a contract services agreement with New Flyer of America, Inc. of Manitoba,
  Canada as a cooperative purchase with the State of California (agreement no.1-19-23-
  17B) in the amount of $5,754,362.78, and authorize a 5% contingency in the amount of
  $287,718.14, for a total not-to-exceed amount of $6,042,080.92, for the purchase and
  delivery of (2) battery electric buses and (2) hydrogen fuel cell buses for the period
   beginning August 20, 2024 and ending December 31, 2026; and
  2)  Approve a contract services agreement with New Flyer of America Inc. of Manitoba,
  Canada, as a cooperative purchase with the State of Washington (agreement no.
  06719-01) in the amount of $17,016,039.84, and authorize a 5% contingency in the
  amount of $850,801.99, for a total not-to-exceed amount of $17,866,841.83, for the
  purchase and delivery of (20) compressed natural gas buses for the period beginning
  August 20, 2024 and ending December 31, 2026.
  9H - STAFF REPORT

  9L.  Transit – Approve Funding Agreement for Visionary Project Seed Funding,
  Appropriate Funds, Authorize Implementation of “Connect Torrance”
  MicroTransit Pilot Project, Approve Contract Services Agreement for “Connect
  Torrance” MicroTransit Pilot Demonstration, and Approve Consulting Services
  Agreement for Data Collection and Analysis. Expenditure: $2,005,390 (Non-
  General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council:
  1) Approve Measure M Grant Agreement #VSF2023001 for Visionary Project Seed
  Funding with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (“LACMTA”); and
  2) Appropriate Measure M Visionary Project Seed Funding grant award in the amount of
  $1,000,000 to a newly created Grant Project; and
  3) Authorize the implementation of a one-year MicroTransit pilot project known as
  “Connect Torrance” to be administered by the City of Torrance Transit Department; and
  4) Approve a contract services agreement with Nomad Transit, LLC of New York, NY to
  provide a turnkey pilot demonstration for an on-demand shared ride service for an
  amount not-to-exceed $1,884,990 following the mutually agreed upon launch date and
  is subject to extension by mutual agreement of the parties on terms to be agreed; and
  5) Approve a consulting services agreement with CALSTART, Inc. of Pasadena, CA for
  the data collection and analysis of the Connect Torrance MicroTransit pilot project for
  an amount not-to-exceed $120,400 following the mutually agreed upon launch date and
  is subject to extension by mutual agreement of the parties on terms to be agreed; and
  6) Appropriate $765,390 to the Transit Enterprise Fund’s fiscal year 2024-25 operating
  budget.
  9L - STAFF REPORT
  9L - STAFF PRESENTATION

  9I.  City Manager – Approve Side Letter Agreement Between Torrance Police Officers
  Association (TPOA) and Management. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council approve a side letter agreement
  between the Torrance Police Officers Association (TPOA) and Management to implement
  Enhanced Recruitment and Retention Incentive Pilot Program.
  9I - STAFF REPORT
  9I - MATERIAL AVAILABLE

  9J.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Amending Resolution No. 2023-144 for
  Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees to Add the Position of Capital
  Projects Construction Superintendent. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council adopt a RESOLUTION amending
  Resolution No. 2023-144 for Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees to add the
  position of Capital Projects Construction Superintendent.
  9J - STAFF REPORT

  9K. Public Works – Approve Second Amendment to Tri-party Agreement for Usage of
  Recycled Water at Torrance Refinery. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed $12,000,000
  (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council approve a second
  amendment to a tri-party agreement with the Torrance Refining Company, LLC of Torrance,
  CA and West Basin Municipal Water District (C2021-027) for an additional amount not-to-
  exceed $12,000,000, for a new not-to-exceed amount of $40,000,000 for the usage of
  recycled water, and to extend the contract term for an additional one-year period beginning
  September 1, 2024 and ending August 31, 2025.
  9K - STAFF REPORT

RECESS
 RECONVENE

10.  HEARINGS

  10A. Community Development – Conduct Public Hearing on Land Use Study 24-00002
  Regarding Proposed Amendments to the Torrance Municipal Code Pertaining to
  Electronic/Digital Billboards, Determine California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) Exemption, and Adopt ORDINANCE Amending Torrance Municipal Code.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1) Conduct a public hearing on Land Use Study 24-00002 regarding proposed
  amendments to the Torrance Municipal Code pertaining to Electronic/Digital Billboards;
  and
  2) Determine that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines; and
  3) Adopt an ORDINANCE amending Torrance Municipal Code Section 911.6.100 entitled
  “Prohibited Signs” of Chapter 11, Article 6, Division 9; repealing Article 10 entitled
  “Enforcement” of Chapter 11, Division 9; adding Article 10 entitled “Electronic/Digital
  Billboards” to Chapter 11, Division 9; adding Article 11 entitled “Enforcement” to
  Chapter 11, Division 9; and
  4) Approve an Ordinance Summary for publication.
  10A - STAFF REPORT PART 1
  10A - STAFF REPORT PART 2
  10A - SUPPLEMENTAL
  10A - STAFF PRESENTATION

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS – None Scheduled.

12.  2ND READING ORDINANCES

  12A. Second and Final Reading of ORDINANCE NO. 3933 amending Division 4 by
  amending section 45.6.6 of the Torrance Municipal Code prohibiting camping in
  public places, amending section 49.2.2 of the Torrance Municipal Code
  prohibiting fires in parks, adding section 45.3.33 to the Torrance Municipal Code
  prohibiting fires in public places, adding section 45.1.9 to the Torrance Municipal
  Code regulating shelters in public places, and adding section 45.1.10 to the
  Torrance Municipal Code prohibiting loitering at bus stop sites and approve an
  Ordinance Summary for publication.
  12A - STAFF REPORT

  12B. Second and Final Reading of ORDINANCE NO. 3934 approving a Development
  Agreement between the City of Torrance and Gable House Development, LLC
  related to a development at 22501 Hawthorne Boulevard, Torrance, California
  (Assessor’s Parcel Number 7368-001-015) and approve an Ordinance Summary
  for publication.
  12B - STAFF REPORT

13.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #2 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) Council Order –
  Mattucci, Sheikh, Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mayor Chen This portion of the meeting
  is reserved for comments on items not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act,
  City Council cannot act on items raised during public comment, but may respond
  briefly to statements made or questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item
  to staff. Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral
  Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you
  step up to the microphone. If presenting handout material to Council, please provide
  11 copies to the City Clerk before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you
  speak.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION
 15.  ADJOURNMENT

  15A. Adjournment of City Council meeting to Tuesday, September 10, 2024, at 5:00
  p.m. for closed session, with regular business commencing at 6:30 p.m. in the
  LeRoy J. Jackson Council Chamber. Tuesday, August 27, 2024 and Tuesday,
  September 3, 2024, are Council Dark Nights.
  15A - STAFF REPORT
